insight.title: Why Small Choices Make Big Decisions Harder
insight.subtitle: How tiny decisions drain the focus you need for important work

sections.text: You spend ten minutes picking a coffee or a font, then feel exhausted when it’s time to sign a contract. Your brain treats every choice as a withdrawal from the same limited account.

This is your decision-making engine at work. It doesn't distinguish between the color of a slide and the direction of a company. Each minor selection adds friction, slowly grinding your judgment to a halt.

By the time you reach high-stakes moments, your clarity is gone. High-performers don't just have better judgment; they have fewer things to judge, preserving their mental energy for the moments that actually matter.
Try this today: When you face a trivial choice today, pick the first decent option in under five seconds.
Quality of thought is determined by the energy you refuse to waste on things that don't matter.

news.title: Indonesia passes law to protect domestic workers after a wait of over 20 years
news.description: Indonesia’s parliament passed a law on Tuesday to protect the rights of domestic workers after more than two decades of deliberations and multiple delays. The bill was first introduced in 2004 to protect the country’s 4.2 million domestic workers, almost 90 per cent of them women, according to data from the Ministry of Manpower.
